Further this Court already discussed and held that the alleged accident was caused on the part of the D.C. Anuradha vs Yashwanth Kumar.G on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99086524/

Under such circumstances, the respondent No.3 is an insurer is liable to pay the compensation and indemnify the 1st respondent.

However, the respondent No.3 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. That apart in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.
This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).
The oral and documentary evidence adduced by petitioners are clearly goes to show that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
Though respondent No.3 examined its official as RW3 but self swearing statements are not sufficient to rebut the evidence put-forth by petitioners.
Therefore I am of the view that, the petitioners have proved that driver of offending mini lorry has caused the accident with rash and  SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.1409/2020 negligent manner and as a result deceased received grievous head injury and succumbed to death.
The documents like Salary certificate, Salary Slip, Bank statements and master role are clearly goes to show that deceased was working as Sales Manager as such company had credited the salary amount through account.
Therefore, only on the basis of non production of appointment letter it cannot be held that deceased was not a employee of aforesaid company.
In case the deceased was self employed or  on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the  established income should be the warrant where  the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An  addition of 25% where the deceased was  between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10%
 where the deceased was between the age of 50  to 60 years, should be regarded as the  necessary method of computation.
The  established income means the income minus the  tax component.
In the case on hand, deceased was aged about 52 D.C. Anuradha vs Yashwanth Kumar.
The judgment reported in 2020 ACJ 759 (National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Birender & others.)
Therefore, after deducting 1/3rd from gross income it would comes at Rs.28,597/-= (42,895- 14,298).
 v)
Thus petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.37,74,804/-=(28,597/-x12xM11) as loss of dependency.
In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & in between National insurance company LTD V/s Pranay Sethi and Ors.
Hence, 3rd respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
The RW3 stated that the offending vehicle was not having valid FC and Permit at the time of accident.
Hence, 3 rd respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
Even 3rd respondent has not taken any pain to call the person by name Suresh T S/o Thotalobayya to prove the Driving License is belongs to person by name Suresh T S/o Thotalobayya not belongs to Suresh H S/o Doddabalaih.
When 3 rd respondent took specific contention it is his burden to prove the said fact.
Therefore, it goes to show that the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Hence, it shows that the owner of offending vehicle was having FC & Permit as on the date of accident and did not violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

1st petitioner is entitled for 70% 2nd petitioner is entitled for 30%

Bengaluru for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on FD periodically.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
